messages:
Alex: Quick question — we're onboarding a partner-managed Postgres that sits in partner VPC (peer IPs 10.55.23.0/24). Do we want to open outbound egress from our app subnets to that CIDR, or is the preferred pattern a VPC Interface Endpoint / PrivateLink? Also: any redaction rules we should apply for connection strings (DB_HOST / DB_URL) in app logs before we request network changes?

Maya: @Alex please include the partner's security contact and the exact FQDN/ARN. High-level: we prefer VPCE or PrivateLink over NAT + 0.0.0.0/0 egress where possible. For logging: strip full DB_URL and only keep obfuscated host/port+masked user. Add a short risk note in the ticket.

Chris: +1 on VPCE if the partner supports it. If they don't, we can do a narrowly scoped egress SG rule or route to a NAT in a dedicated egress subnet. My recommended approach:
- Try Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink) first
- If not possible, create an egress-only SG rule to 10.55.23.0/24 on port 5432 and put an explicit expiration tag (ttl:48h) for audit

Example terraform snippet for a VPCE we use internally:
```hcl
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "partner_postgres" {
  vpc_id            = var.vpc_id
  service_name      = "com.amazonaws.vpce.partner-postgres.example"
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  subnet_ids        = var.private_subnet_ids
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.sg_egress.id]
}
```

Jordan: FYI our app currently logs the full JDBC URL in debug logs. I'll send a PR to redact it (mask host and user) and switch debug-level DB connection logs off in prod. Who needs to approve the logging change?

Maya: @Jordan please open a PR in infra-config and add a link to the partner's security questionnaire. Security review required: data-protection and network. Tag `team:security` and `policy:data-protection` in the PR description. We'll do a quick eval — if PRs touch logging code, we also need a short test plan showing no creds in logs.

Alex: thanks — I'll kick off the ticket with partner contact + security questionnaire attached. Plan: try VPCE first; if partner can't support it, request temporary SG egress rule with TTL and manual review in 48h.

sec-approvals-bot: Approval requested: network-egress to 10.55.23.0/24 (port 5432) — status: pending review by team:security. Ticket: INFRA-4321.

Chris: One more note — if we go SG egress route, avoid attaching broad NAT routes across all private subnets. Prefer a dedicated egress ENI or an egress-only subnet with monitoring (flow logs + restricted route table).

Jordan: PR created: https://git.internal/infra-config/pulls/1284 — includes redaction middleware and a test that asserts DB_URL is masked in logs. @Maya can you review?

Maya: Reviewing now. Once the PR is green and the partner confirms inability to support VPCE, security will sign off for the temporary egress rule (with TTL, risk note, and audit log requirement). :white_check_mark:

Alex: Awesome. I'll update INFRA-4321 with plan + cost center + owner. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
